text:
support: seeing a spike of 503s across hosted API since 09:12 UTC. multiple customers reporting timeouts and gateway errors. sample request ids: req_34a9, req_b7f2. raising here for triage.
sre-oncall: on it — checking upstream runner pools and node health. any auth/billing correlation?
support: none. errors are 503/gateway upstream aborted. traces show upstream inference worker resets.
alice: I see container respawn loop on pool-gpu-us-west-2-prod-12. docker exit code=139 (segfault). grabbing last logs now.
alice: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:33Z] infer-runner[1228]: ARRIVE kv_prefetch batch=64 prefetch=4 mem_usage=87%
[2026-03-17T09:12:34Z] infer-runner[1228]: CUDA error: illegal instruction (pc=0x7f82fd3a)
[2026-03-17T09:12:34Z] infer-runner[1228]: segfault (signal 11) -- dumping core
```
ben: same pattern in metrics — prefetch and batch size spike, GPU memory climbs to ~98% then reset -> container restart. looks like OOM followed by illegal-instruction crash in quantized attention kernel.
sre-oncall: mitigation in progress: scaled pool + spun up 6 warm workers in us-west-2. enabled fallback route for non-critical traffic to cpu-small-model.
deploy-bot: route update applied: fallback-model=cpu-small for plan=free, canary=10% at 09:18 UTC.
support: sent interim status to affected customers and updated status.redwood.ai with "investigating - upstream worker crashes".
alice: collecting core, stack, and nvcrash logs — uploading to s3: s3://redwood-debug/1766007890/core-and-logs.tar.gz
alice: repro notes so far: reproduce locally with model v2-quant, batch_size=64, prefetch=4, long context (~2048 tokens) -> triggers memory surge then crash. command: 
```
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d @large_batch_payload.json
```
ben: short-term mitigations: cap prefetch to 2 on quant runtimes, backpressure when GPU mem > 85%, reject batches >32 for v2-quant. will push config change to canary.
sre-oncall: hotfix plan: roll out batch-size cap for quant runtime (canary 10% -> 100% if stable). create follow-up incident ticket with timeline & customer impact.
support: acknowledged. please post ETA for resolution and any required customer action.
ben: ETA for full mitigation ~30-45m pending canary. will update.
sre-oncall: creating incident ticket RED-INC-2026-176600 for postmortem and action items.
support: thanks — keep updates concise here, will consolidate for CS team.
